title: Tier-integrity exception ledger
description: Schema for config/tier-integrity.jsonc (sc-15799) — the declared above-tier residency exceptions to the invariant 'no component is resident above the user's selected quant tier unless a declared, measured exception says otherwise'. The normative statement lives in docs/memory-strategy-contract.md ('Tier integrity'); the executable rule is gen_core::tier_integrity. scripts/check-tier-integrity.mjs APPLIES this schema to the ledger on every run (its `schemaErrors` walks the subset used here) and adds the cross-checks a JSON Schema cannot express: that the model is a real catalog entry, that residentTier is strictly above every tier in appliesToTiers, that appliesToTiers names only hosted tiers, that a declared `backends` lane is one the catalog entry actually has a block for, that no two rows claim the same (model, component, lane), and the per-(model, component) unmeasured ratchet. NOTE (sc-15799 review): this file was originally IDE-only and unenforced, which is how it drifted to draft-07 with a sceneworks.dev $id while every sibling schema requires draft 2020-12 and a sceneworks.local id — scripts/check-scaffold.mjs now pins both conventions for this schema alongside the manifest schemas. Its load-bearing contribution is additionalProperties:false: before it was applied, a misspelled key such as `backend` for `backends` was silently ignored.

exceptions.description: Every above-tier residency in the catalog that meets the declaration threshold stated in the ledger's own header. An EMPTY array is not the same as a conformant catalog — it means the audit was lost, and the checker rejects it.

model.description: Catalog entry id in config/manifests/builtin.models.jsonc. The checker rejects an id that has no entry.

component.description: Which component is resident above tier. The row uniqueness key is (model, component, BACKEND LANE) — a component whose residency genuinely differs per lane is split into one row per lane, and the checker rejects two rows that claim the same lane for the same pair. The unmeasured ratchet is keyed on (model, component) alone, so splitting a row per lane does not widen the amnesty.

residentTier.description: The precision the component is ACTUALLY resident at. Must be strictly above every tier in appliesToTiers on the fidelity ladder f32 > bf16 > q8 > q4 = nvfp4 (int8-convrot ranks with q8) — an 'exception' at or below the selected tier is a mistake, not an exception, and the checker says so.

appliesToTiers.description: The SELECTED tiers on which this component is above tier. Never includes a tier at or below residentTier, and — where the entry publishes per-tier download variants — never a tier the entry does not host, since an exception for a tier nobody can select is dead.

backends.description: Which lanes carry this residency. OMIT for both. Declare it when the lanes genuinely differ — the mage transformerHead floor, for example, exists only in mlx-gen-mage; candle-gen-mage has no floor symbol at all, so a q4 render there really is uniformly q4. THE SAME DECLARED TIER CAN YIELD DIFFERENT RESIDENCY PER BACKEND, so residentTier is a per-lane fact: sensenova_u1_8b's vision conv kernels and fm_head are bf16 under mlx-gen-sensenova but f32 under candle-gen-sensenova, which widens every dense leaf it multiplies against an f32 activation (candle-gen-sensenova/src/quant.rs::get_f32, sc-14249). Such a component is declared as one row per lane. Enforced, not advisory: the checker validates the lane names, requires each declared lane to be one the catalog entry actually has a block for, keys row uniqueness on it, and publishes it as a column in docs/generated/tier-integrity.md.

cause.description: packing-exception: a deliberate quality DECISION — the component is not packed because packing it measurably hurts. backend-capability: the backend cannot serve the on-disk format and upcasts; packing cannot fix it, so it needs a compute path or a re-host. structural: there is nothing quantizable at all (all-conv stacks, leaves the loader folds away). The distinction is load-bearing, not cosmetic: a `structural` row is written out of what a measurement story could ever fix, so labelling a choice `structural` hides it.

reason.description: One sentence, in the terms the provider itself uses.

state.description: measured: costGb (or costBytes) is a real in-tree number. unmeasured: no isolated component cost exists in the tree yet. UNMEASURED IS RATIONED — legal only for the (model, component) pairs enumerated in scripts/check-tier-integrity.mjs's GRANDFATHERED_UNMEASURED, whose size is pinned by GRANDFATHERED_UNMEASURED_COUNT so any change is a reviewed two-place edit. That list lives in the checker, not here, so editing this file cannot widen the amnesty.

costGb.description: The isolated cost of holding this component above tier, in GB. Required (and positive) when state is measured — an exception whose cost nobody knows is undeclared in the only way that matters.

costBytes.description: Alternative to costGb when the in-tree number is a byte count.

source.description: file:line (or file plus a quoted phrase) where the FACT is recorded in-tree — and the number too, when measured. Required on every row, measured or not: an undeclared cost is tolerable while it is owed, an uncited fact is not.

owedBy.description: The Shortcut story that owes the measurement. Required when state is unmeasured.

note.description: Anything a future reader needs that the one-sentence reason cannot hold: why a number was NOT borrowed from a nearby total, what a re-cause changed and why, which sibling finding would let the row move to another cause.
